docs.title: Build a data platform, one verified step at a time
docs.text:
A hands-on lab for learning Linux, Kubernetes, data engineering and AI engineering. Follow the build from a Windows laptop to a working platform, with commands, explanations and screenshots from the actual setup.

Start with the foundation See the latest progress

docs.title: The lab at a glance
docs.text: Layer Technology Virtual machines Hyper-V on Windows Operating system Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.8 Kubernetes kubeadm, CRI-O and Calico Planned CI GitHub Actions runner and a local registry Planned workloads Data pipelines, notebooks and AI experiments

docs.title: Follow the build
docs.text:
1. Set up Git and GitHub.
  2. Create the Hyper-V network.
  3. Install RHEL.
  4. Verify networking, SSH and package access.
  5. Prepare the Kubernetes node.
  6. Bootstrap the control plane and configure Calico.
  7. Create the first worker VM.
  8. Explore the CI and registry plan.

docs.title: Evidence, not just instructions
docs.text:
The progress register separates verified outcomes from planned work. The screenshot index contains 33 reviewed captures, including intermediate failures and their resolution. Commands describe a guided build; read their context before rerunning them on an existing system.

This is an independent personal lab using synthetic data, not a production deployment.

docs.title: Purpose and execution location
docs.text:
Run these commands in normal Windows PowerShell. The source repository lives on Windows because Hyper-V is managed from Windows. Linux commands will run inside the future RHEL VMs. WSL is not required for this repository.

This guide records the completed sequence; the repository already exists. Do not repeat repository creation or overwrite an existing .gitignore.

docs.title: Create and enter the working folder
docs.text:
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path "$env:USERPROFILE\Documents\AI Engineering\data-platform-lab" -Force
Set-Location "$env:USERPROFILE\Documents\AI Engineering\data-platform-lab"
git --version

USERPROFILE locates the current Windows user's home folder. New-Item creates the directory; Set-Location selects it as the working directory. git --version confirms Git is available. Opening a terminal does not automatically put it inside the repository.

docs.title: Exclusions, identity and the first commit
docs.text:
The committed .gitignore excludes credentials, virtual disks, ISOs, generated data and local artifacts. Review it before adding new types of artifacts. Ignore rules do not remove files already tracked by Git and are not a secret scanner.

git init -b main
git var GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT
git status --short
git add -- .gitignore
git commit -m "Initialize repository with exclusions for secrets and local artifacts"
git status
  • init -b main creates local history with an initial branch called main.
  • var GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT checks the name and email recorded on commits. A GitHub noreply address can be used for public commit privacy.
  • status --short shows changed and untracked files; ?? means untracked.
  • add -- .gitignore selects that exact file for the next snapshot.
  • commit -m saves the selected content locally with an explanatory message.

docs.title: Install GitHub CLI and authenticate
docs.text:
Git tracks local history; GitHub hosts a remote copy. gh is a separate command-line client for GitHub. A WSL installation does not automatically make it available in Windows PowerShell.

winget install --id GitHub.cli --exact --source winget

Reopen PowerShell after installation so the new command path is available.

gh --version
gh auth login --hostname github.com --git-protocol https --web

Complete authentication in the browser and allow Git authentication when prompted. Device codes and access tokens must not be recorded in this repo.

docs.title: Create the public remote and push
docs.text:
From the local project folder:

gh repo create data-platform-lab --public --source . --remote origin --push
gh repo view --json nameWithOwner,url,visibility
git status -sb

--source . uses the current repository. origin is the saved name for its remote address. --public publishes committed content for anyone to read. --push uploads the initial commit.

The remote is https://github.com/Sabareh/data-platform-lab.

docs.title: Documentation workflow
docs.text:
The original README was committed with:

git add -- README.md
git commit -m "Document lab architecture, verified progress and networking blocker"
git push origin main

For subsequent updates, inspect content first, stage named files and review the staged diff before committing:

git status --short
git diff
# Stage only the intended files with git add -- <paths>.
git diff --cached
# Commit with a message describing the final change, then push.

New untracked files do not appear in ordinary git diff; read them directly or inspect them after staging. A clean working tree means local files match the current commit. It does not prove that someone has not changed GitHub since the last fetch.

docs.text:

docs.title: What we are building
docs.text:
Run this guide's Hyper-V configuration commands in Administrator PowerShell. The user created a dedicated internal switch, assigned a gateway address and enabled NAT. No VM-to-internet connectivity test has been completed yet.

Future RHEL Kubernetes nodes
          |
reservoir-lab-switch (Internal)
          |
Windows virtual adapter: 192.168.200.1/24
          |
reservoir-lab-nat
          |
Windows network connection -> home router -> internet

An internal switch connects VMs to each other and the host. It does not provide internet access on its own. The gateway is the host's address used by VMs to reach other networks. NAT translates outbound connections and tracks replies so multiple VMs can share the host's internet connection.

NAT does not provide DHCP or automatically make the gateway a DNS server. Each guest will need an address, subnet, gateway and DNS configuration. The gateway is also not a Satellite/package-repository server.

docs.title: Inspect before creating
docs.text:
These commands only read configuration:

Get-VM | Select-Object Name, State, CPUUsage, MemoryAssigned
Get-VMSwitch | Select-Object Name, SwitchType, NetAdapterInterfaceDescription
Get-NetIPAddress -AddressFamily IPv4 | Select-Object InterfaceAlias, IPAddress, PrefixLength
Get-NetNat | Select-Object Name, InternalIPInterfaceAddressPrefix

The initial VM listing was empty. Existing switches were Default Switch and WSL (Hyper-V firewall), both Internal. The observed network ranges were:

Use Observed subnet Home Wi-Fi 192.168.100.0/24 Default Switch 172.19.112.0/20 WSL 172.24.224.0/20

Get-NetNat returned no entries. This does not mean that Windows-managed Default Switch or WSL networking has no address translation of its own. The lab range does not overlap the observed interface subnets; VPN or future network routes must also be considered if connectivity changes.

docs.title: Create the switch
docs.text:
New-VMSwitch -Name "reservoir-lab-switch" -SwitchType Internal

The reservoir-lab network names were chosen before the Git repository was named data-platform-lab. They are retained to match the deployed objects.

docs.title: Troubleshooting the initial failure
docs.text:
The first attempt failed with:

Internal miniport create failed
Cannot create a file when that file already exists. (0x800700B7)

The following read-only inspections were performed:

Get-VMSwitch | Select-Object Name, Id, SwitchType
Get-NetAdapter -IncludeHidden | Select-Object Name, InterfaceDescription, ifIndex, Status
Get-PnpDevice -Class Net | Select-Object Status, FriendlyName, InstanceId

Findings:

  • No switch or adapter named reservoir-lab-switch was listed.
  • The listed Hyper-V switch extension devices reported OK.
  • Unknown RAS/Bluetooth entries did not establish the cause and were not removed.
  • A Windows restart was recommended before retrying. The conversation does not explicitly confirm that a restart occurred.
  • The subsequent New-VMSwitch command succeeded and reported Internal.

Outcome: creation succeeded on retry. Root cause remains unknown; do not claim a proven duplicate-device repair or delete unrelated network devices.

docs.title: Identify the adapter and assign the gateway
docs.text:
Get-NetAdapter -Name "vEthernet (reservoir-lab-switch)" | Select-Object Name, ifIndex, Status
New-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias "vEthernet (reservoir-lab-switch)" -IPAddress 192.168.200.1 -PrefixLength 24

The adapter was reported Up. /24 is equivalent to 255.255.255.0: .0 identifies the subnet, .255 is its broadcast address and .1 is the chosen Windows gateway. VM addresses will be assigned later without duplicates.

The assignment initially showed Tentative in ActiveStore and Invalid in PersistentStore. We checked the operational state rather than assuming failure from the immediate output:

Get-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias "vEthernet (reservoir-lab-switch)" -AddressFamily IPv4 -PolicyStore ActiveStore | Select-Object IPAddress, PrefixLength, AddressState

Observed result:

IPAddress       PrefixLength AddressState
192.168.200.1              24 Preferred

Preferred means the address is usable. Adapter index 57 was observed, but indices can change, so the commands use the adapter name.

docs.title: Configure and verify NAT
docs.text:
New-NetNat -Name "reservoir-lab-nat" -InternalIPInterfaceAddressPrefix "192.168.200.0/24"
Get-NetNat -Name "reservoir-lab-nat" | Select-Object Name, InternalIPInterfaceAddressPrefix, Active

Observed result:

Name               InternalIPInterfaceAddressPrefix Active
reservoir-lab-nat   192.168.200.0/24                   True

This confirms configuration, not end-to-end internet connectivity. Existing objects should be inspected rather than recreated. Microsoft documents a single internal NAT prefix limitation for WinNAT; do not add unrelated NAT objects or remove existing ones blindly.

docs.title: Remaining validation
docs.text:
• Confirm configuration survives a host restart.
  • Assign guest network settings and test gateway reachability.
  • Test DNS resolution and outbound HTTPS from the first guest.
  • Later, test node-to-node communication.
  • Choose Kubernetes Pod and Service ranges without overlaps.

Kubernetes node networking is this VM network. Pod and Service networking will be configured separately once the Linux nodes are ready.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text: Microsoft: Set up a Hyper-V NAT network

docs.title: RHEL installation media and first VM
Decision and limits
docs.text:
RHEL was selected to practise the operating-system tools used in the reference environment. The reference environment's exact major/minor version is unknown. RHEL 9.8 is a lab choice, not a confirmed production match.

Use a personal Red Hat Developer Subscription for Individuals, subject to its current terms. Red Hat describes it as no-cost, self-supported access for up to 16 physical or virtual systems. This does not establish support coverage for the planned upstream Kubernetes installation.

docs.title: Capacity checks
docs.text:
Run in Windows PowerShell:

Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem | Select-Object @{Name='TotalRAM_GB';Expression={[math]::Round($_.TotalVisibleMemorySize / 1MB, 1)}}, @{Name='FreeRAM_GB';Expression={[math]::Round($_.FreePhysicalMemory / 1MB, 1)}}
Get-Volume -DriveLetter C | Select-Object DriveLetter, @{Name='SizeGB';Expression={[math]::Round($_.Size / 1GB, 1)}}, @{Name='FreeGB';Expression={[math]::Round($_.SizeRemaining / 1GB, 1)}}

Observed before downloading/installing:

Measurement Value Total usable RAM 31.7 Available RAM at the time 18.7 C: capacity 476 C: free space at the time 198.9

The command labels say GB; these PowerShell conversions use binary units (GiB). Windows reports the memory fields in KiB, hence dividing by 1MB (1,048,576) converts those values to GiB. These are historical measurements, not reservations or a guarantee of current free capacity.

docs.title: Keep VM files outside Git
docs.text:
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path "$env:USERPROFILE\HyperV\data-platform-lab" -Force

Source lives under Documents\AI Engineering\data-platform-lab; virtual disks live under HyperV\data-platform-lab. ISOs remain in Downloads.

docs.title: Obtain and verify the ISO
docs.text:
Download the RHEL 9.8 x86_64 DVD ISO from the official Red Hat page after signing in. x86_64 matches this Intel laptop. The DVD ISO supplies local installation packages; boot-only media depends more on a network source.

IDM initially captured auth.htm pages rather than the ISO. This suggested an authentication redirect problem, but the exact cause was not verified. The final ISO was subsequently downloaded successfully. Do not save signed download URLs, account tokens or authentication pages in this repository.

Locate and hash the downloaded file:

Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads" -Filter '*rhel*.iso' -File -Recurse | Select-Object FullName, @{Name='SizeGB';Expression={[math]::Round($_.Length / 1GB, 2)}}
Get-FileHash -LiteralPath "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\rhel-9.8-x86_64-dvd.iso" -Algorithm SHA256 | Format-List

Verified filename: rhel-9.8-x86_64-dvd.iso, approximately 14.47 GiB.

The observed SHA-256 matches the value published on Red Hat's download page:

c0dd53b73406b85b40d6168d1748e605d71361b2992d282c408b7d7d2e1d2c80

Uppercase/lowercase does not change a hexadecimal hash. Compare the checksum for the exact version, architecture and image type; another ISO has another expected hash. This is an integrity comparison against the vendor's HTTPS page, not a separately performed signature verification.

docs.title: Create the VM
docs.text:
Run in Administrator PowerShell. These creation commands have already been executed in this lab. Do not rerun them blindly.

New-VM -Name "lab-control-01" -Generation 2 -MemoryStartupBytes 3GB -NewVHDPath "$env:USERPROFILE\HyperV\data-platform-lab\lab-control-01\os.vhdx" -NewVHDSizeBytes 40GB -Path "$env:USERPROFILE\HyperV\data-platform-lab" -SwitchName "reservoir-lab-switch"
  • Generation 2 provides UEFI virtual firmware.
  • 3 GB is the initial startup memory allocation.
  • NewVHDSizeBytes gives the expanding virtual disk a maximum logical size of 40 GB. Its host file grows as data is written; it does not immediately reserve all 40 GB of physical disk capacity.
  • SwitchName connects the VM to the prepared private network.
  • New-VM creates the machine but does not start it or install Linux.

docs.title: Configure CPU and Secure Boot while the VM is off
docs.text:
Set-VMProcessor -VMName "lab-control-01" -Count 2
Set-VMFirmware -VMName "lab-control-01" -EnableSecureBoot On -SecureBootTemplate MicrosoftUEFICertificateAuthority

Two virtual processors share the host's physical CPU resources. The firmware template permits supported Linux bootloaders while keeping Secure Boot enabled.

docs.title: Attach media and select DVD boot
docs.text:
Add-VMDvdDrive -VMName "lab-control-01" -Path "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\rhel-9.8-x86_64-dvd.iso"
Set-VMFirmware -VMName "lab-control-01" -FirstBootDevice (Get-VMDvdDrive -VMName "lab-control-01")
vmconnect.exe localhost "lab-control-01"

Add-VMDvdDrive inserts the ISO as a virtual DVD. FirstBootDevice chooses that DVD before the empty virtual disk. vmconnect.exe opens the machine's console on this host. Click Start and press a key if prompted to boot DVD.

The user confirmed reaching the RHEL installer boot menu. The next instruction was to choose Install Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.8. Selecting it starts the installer; it does not alone prove that Linux has been installed.

docs.title: Installer configuration (VM console)
docs.text: These are graphical installer steps, not PowerShell commands. The final Installation Summary screenshot confirms the selections below. No passwords or account-registration secrets are stored in this guide.

docs.title: Software, language and time
docs.text:
Starting state: Server with GUI, New York time zone and incomplete account settings. These are historical defaults, not the final lab configuration.

  1. Select Install Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.8 in the boot menu.
  2. The resulting summary shows English (United States) language support and English (US) keyboard. Choose a different keyboard if needed for your hardware.
  3. Open Software Selection, select Server, leave optional add-ons unselected, then click Done.
  4. Open Time & Date, select Africa / Nairobi, then click Done.

The graphical installer can install a system without a graphical desktop. Server was chosen over Server with GUI to conserve resources and practise terminal/SSH administration. Minimal Install was considered, but Server was selected as the broader starting environment. Neither installs Kubernetes. Application dashboards will later be accessed through the Windows browser.

The time-zone setting controls local time display; it does not prove clock synchronisation. NTP/chrony was verified later in the node preparation guide.

Selection step: Server without a desktop. Container Management and the other optional add-ons were not needed for this initial OS installation.

docs.title: Administrator account
docs.text:
Intermediate step: software selection is saved, but no user will yet be created. The later final summary confirms administrator sabare. The root password-entry screenshot is omitted; no password screenshots are needed.

The user created sabare. The final summary explicitly states that administrator sabare will be created. Administrator membership permits privileged commands through sudo after installation; this still needs a post-installation test.

A root password was also set privately. The setup instruction was to uncheck Allow root SSH login with password before saving. The user reported that step done, but the effective SSH policy must be checked after installation. Use the named administrator for routine access and keep both passwords out of Git, screenshots and command history.

docs.title: Static network settings
docs.text:
Open Network & Host Name:

Before configuration: the adapter is detected but switched off, with no address shown. This alone is not evidence of a Hyper-V network fault.

  1. Enter lab-control-01 in Host Name and click Apply.
  2. Select Ethernet (eth0) and click Configure.
  3. On IPv4 Settings, choose Manual and add the following settings.
Field Value Explanation Address 192.168.200.10 Fixed address for this VM on the lab network Netmask 255.255.255.0 Same subnet size as /24 Gateway 192.168.200.1 Windows lab adapter; routes outbound traffic through NAT DNS servers 1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8 Public name resolvers for this home lab Search domains Empty No internal DNS search domain configured yet
  1. On General, enable automatic connection when available, if shown.
  2. Save and turn the Ethernet toggle ON.
  3. Confirm the displayed address and DNS settings, then click Done.

The adapter initially remained off after saving. Turning it on resolved the disconnected state. The user reported address 192.168.200.10 and the DNS servers displayed; the final summary confirms Connected: eth0.

Intermediate step: hostname application succeeded, but the Ethernet toggle still needed to be turned on. This is not a screenshot of a working connection.

No successful DNS query, outbound HTTPS test or post-reboot persistence test has yet been recorded. The hostname does not automatically create a DNS record on Windows. Public DNS is a local lab choice, not a production setting.

docs.title: Installation destination and final review
docs.text:
Select the 40 GiB Microsoft virtual disk (sda) under Installation Destination, choose Automatic storage configuration and click Done. The screenshot shows encryption unchecked. The final partition layout has not been inspected, so no specific LVM, filesystem or swap sizes are claimed.

Storage selection: sda is the VM's 40 GiB virtual disk. The displayed 1.97 MiB free prompted further review; its meaning was not independently established. The subsequent summary accepted the configuration.

The disk page displayed only 1.97 MiB free. That number was initially treated as evidence of existing partitions, but it alone did not establish a fault. The user clarified that no Reclaim Space dialog was present and provided a summary with no destination warning and Begin Installation enabled. No manual partition deletion or reclaim operation is confirmed.

Final summary observed:

Item Displayed state Software Selection Server Installation Source Local media Time & Date Africa/Nairobi Installation Destination Automatic partitioning selected; no warning icon Network Connected: eth0 Root Password Root password is set User Creation Administrator sabare will be created Connect to Red Hat Not registered KDUMP Enabled Security Profile No profile selected

The summary also displayed an SMT-enabled warning. No CPU/SMT configuration change was made in response. No security profile selection does not imply that SELinux or the firewall is disabled; their actual state will be checked.

Evidence: final settings before Begin Installation. The Not registered label is historical; registration was completed later. This screen alone does not prove installation completion.

The user clicked Begin Installation, subsequently reported completion, and reached the installed RHEL login prompt after reboot. See the first-boot guide for screenshots and verification.

docs.title: Pending installation work
docs.text:
• Verify whether installation media remains attached and adjust disk boot order if needed.
  • Inspect effective SSH policy; named-user login and sudo have succeeded.
  • Verify OS version, storage layout, swap, SELinux and firewall state.
  • Verify time synchronisation; addressing, routing, DNS and HTTPS passed first-boot checks.
  • Complete the metadata-download check; registration and SSH login were reported successful.
  • Review actual VM configuration and resource consumption.
  • Create workers later; no worker VMs or Kubernetes cluster are verified yet.

The proposed 3 GB allocation may need adjustment if the installer or workloads require more memory. Do not disable SELinux or the firewall merely to bypass an unexplained installation/networking problem.

docs.title: First boot, networking, SSH and package access
docs.text: Evidence captured during the guided build on 2026-10-14. Commands labelled RHEL run inside the VM, either through its console or an established SSH session. Windows commands run in PowerShell. Check the prompt before typing.

docs.title: 1. Confirm the installed system boots
docs.text:
After installation, select Reboot System. The observed result was the RHEL 9.8 login prompt for lab-control-01, rather than the installation menu.

Evidence: the installed system reaches its login prompt. The on-screen Cockpit activation suggestion was not executed as part of this milestone.

Log in locally as sabare using the privately chosen password. Linux terminal password prompts do not echo characters or asterisks.

Evidence: named-user console login works. This screen predates the SSH test and should not be used as proof of remote authentication.

docs.title: 2. Verify administrator access and network settings
docs.text:
Run in RHEL, one command at a time:

sudo whoami
ip -br address
ip route
Command Purpose Observed result sudo whoami Test ability to run a command as administrator root ip -br address Brief interface and address listing eth0 UP, 192.168.200.10/24 ip route Inspect traffic-routing rules Default via 192.168.200.1, device eth0

Evidence: address and gateway settings survived the installation reboot. The local subnet route lets nodes communicate directly; the default route handles destinations outside that subnet. This does not by itself prove internet access. The visible IPv6 address is a local lab link-local address.

docs.title: 3. Test name resolution and HTTPS separately
docs.text:
Run in RHEL:

getent ahostsv4 www.redhat.com
curl -I --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 30 https://www.redhat.com

getent uses the configured name-resolution system. The observed IPv4 response was 23.42.240.53; it may differ on another run. Repeated STREAM, DGRAM and RAW entries are normal socket-type listings.

Evidence: the corrected hostname lookup returns records. The preceding mistyped lookup produced no result; the successful command uses www.redhat.com.

curl -I retrieves headers rather than the page body, with bounded connection and total timeouts. It returned HTTP/2 301, redirecting to https://www.redhat.com/en. This demonstrates an HTTPS response from that endpoint with normal certificate checking, not access to every internet site.

The HTTP-header screenshot is intentionally omitted because it includes Set-Cookie values. The result is transcribed above without those values.

docs.title: 4. Check SSH on the guest and from Windows
docs.text:
Run in RHEL:

systemctl is-active sshd

It returned active. sshd is the server accepting encrypted terminal connections; this command only checks its current service state.

Run in Windows PowerShell:

Test-NetConnection -ComputerName 192.168.200.10 -Port 22

Evidence: Windows reached port 22 through reservoir-lab-switch, from 192.168.200.1 to 192.168.200.10. TCP success is separate from SSH authentication.

docs.title: 5. Verify the host identity and log in
docs.text:
In the trusted Hyper-V RHEL console, obtain the server public-key fingerprint:

sudo ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub

This reads an existing public key; it does not create a new key. The first attempt contained a command-name typo; rerunning ssh-keygen correctly worked.

From Windows PowerShell:

ssh sabare@192.168.200.10

Compare the ED25519 SHA-256 fingerprint with the console output before accepting the first connection. Accept only a match. Windows then stores the host key in known_hosts. Enter the local sabare password when prompted; this is not the Red Hat website account password.

docs.title: Authentication troubleshooting
docs.text:
The first login failed after password attempts, although TCP connectivity worked. Inspect the server log from the already-open RHEL console:

sudo journalctl -u sshd --since "15 minutes ago" --no-pager -n 30

This selects recent SSH service logs without entering a pager. The output showed pam_unix authentication failures and failed passwords for sabare; it did not establish a network failure or an explicit account lock.

Troubleshooting evidence: the guest received the Windows connection but rejected password authentication. These are local lab addresses and usernames; no password is printed. Later login success was reported by the user.

The user changed their own password in the console with:

passwd

This prompts privately for the current password and the new password twice. It is a troubleshooting action, not a command to run on every login. No password is recorded here. After retrying SSH, the user confirmed login worked with the new password. The exact cause of the original mismatch (for example typing or keyboard layout) was not proven.

docs.title: 6. Register with Red Hat
docs.text:
In the RHEL SSH session:

sudo subscription-manager identity

The result was that the system was not yet registered. The user then ran:

sudo subscription-manager register

Enter the local sabare password at a sudo prompt, then the Red Hat login ID and account password at the registration prompts. Do not place credentials in command arguments, Git or screenshots. Registration was reported successful; system UUID and account/organisation details are not included in this repo.

docs.title: 7. Verify repository configuration, then metadata access
docs.text:
In RHEL:

sudo dnf repolist --enabled

The user confirmed BaseOS and AppStream are enabled. These supply core OS packages and additional application/tool packages. An enabled listing alone does not prove repository metadata can be downloaded.

The next command was issued as the metadata-access test:

sudo dnf makecache --refresh

makecache builds the local repository-metadata cache; --refresh expires cached metadata before the operation so DNF checks the repositories again. It does not install or upgrade packages. The user subsequently supplied "Metadata cache created", confirming success.

docs.title: Continued preparation
docs.text: Storage, updates, fixed VM memory, persistent swap disablement, time synchronisation, SELinux/firewall inspection, CRI-O and Kubernetes package installation are documented in node preparation. Effective SSH policy and cluster deployment remain pending.

docs.title: Preparing the first RHEL Kubernetes node
docs.text: Recorded 2026-10-14 (Africa/Nairobi). These commands document the guided build; do not rerun configuration writes blindly. Unless labelled Windows, commands run in the RHEL SSH session as sabare, with sudo where required.

docs.title: Current outcome
docs.text: This chapter records preparation through package installation. Subsequent runtime checks, successful cluster initialisation and operator readiness are documented in control-plane and Calico preparation.

docs.title: 1. Update RHEL and inspect storage
docs.text:
sudo dnf makecache --refresh
sudo dnf upgrade --refresh --assumeno
sudo dnf upgrade --refresh
sudo reboot

Metadata retrieval succeeded. The preview proposed four installations and 220 upgrades, approximately 1 GB to download. --assumeno intentionally ends with Operation aborted; it is a preview, not a failed installation. The actual upgrade subsequently reported Complete! in shared terminal output.

Reconnect from Windows using ssh sabare@192.168.200.10, then inspect:

uname -r
lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,TYPE,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINTS
df -h / /boot /boot/efi
swapon --show
free -h

The running kernel became 5.14.0-687.57.1.el9_8.x86_64. The 40 GiB disk has an EFI partition, an XFS boot partition and LVM logical volumes for root and swap. Root had approximately 33 GiB available. LVM separates logical storage allocation from physical partitions; XFS is the filesystem used for root.

docs.title: 2. Correct the VM memory allocation
docs.text:
The guest initially reported only 489 MiB RAM. Hyper-V inspection showed Dynamic Memory enabled, a 512 MiB minimum and 3072 MiB startup allocation. Samples were taken at different times; their memory numbers need not match exactly.

Shut down gracefully from RHEL:

sudo shutdown -h now

In Windows PowerShell, confirm the VM is Off before changing memory:

Get-VM -Name "lab-control-01" | Select-Object Name, State
Set-VMMemory -VMName "lab-control-01" -DynamicMemoryEnabled $false -StartupBytes 3GB
Get-VMMemory -VMName "lab-control-01" | Select-Object DynamicMemoryEnabled, @{Name='StartupMiB';Expression={$_.Startup / 1MB}}
Start-VM -Name "lab-control-01"

The user confirmed False and 3072. After boot, RHEL showed about 2.6 GiB usable RAM. Fixed allocation provides a predictable baseline for this node.

docs.title: 3. Disable swap persistently
docs.text:
This lab uses a no-swap Kubernetes baseline. Kubernetes can support explicitly configured swap use, but that is outside this initial setup. Disabling swap does not create more RAM: workloads still need appropriate memory limits.

sudo swapoff -a
swapon --show
cat /etc/fstab
sudo cp -a /etc/fstab "/etc/fstab.before-disable-swap.$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
sudo sed -i '\|^/dev/mapper/rhel_lab--control--01-swap[[:space:]]|s|^|# Disabled for Kubernetes: |' /etc/fstab
sudo findmnt --verify --verbose
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo reboot

The edit targets the exact swap line observed on this VM. The backup preserves the original mount configuration. findmnt validates it; daemon-reload refreshes systemd's generated units. The swap logical volume was not deleted.

After reconnecting:

swapon --show
free -h
systemctl --type=swap --state=active

Verified after reboot: no active swap devices, Swap 0B, zero active swap units.

docs.title: 4. Inspect security, cgroups and time
docs.text:
timedatectl
systemctl is-active chronyd
chronyc tracking
chronyc sources -v
getenforce
systemctl is-active firewalld
sudo firewall-cmd --get-active-zones
sudo firewall-cmd --list-all
stat -fc %T /sys/fs/cgroup
rpm -q podman containerd containerd.io cri-o

Initial results: chronyd inactive, SELinux Enforcing, firewalld active on eth0 in the public zone, and cgroup2fs. Podman was installed; CRI-O was not yet installed. The chronyc error 506 Cannot talk to daemon occurred because chronyd was stopped.

Enable time synchronisation and inspect it after allowing time to contact servers:

sudo systemctl enable --now chronyd
systemctl is-enabled chronyd
systemctl is-active chronyd
chronyc tracking
chronyc sources -v
timedatectl

Verified: enabled, active, Leap status Normal, a selected ^* time source and System clock synchronized: yes. Correct time helps certificate validation and correlating logs across nodes. SELinux and firewalld were not disabled at this stage. Firewalld was later disabled during Calico preparation.

docs.title: 5. Prepare kernel modules and packet forwarding
docs.text:
sudo tee /etc/modules-load.d/k8s.conf > /dev/null <<'EOF'
overlay
br_netfilter
EOF
sudo modprobe overlay
sudo modprobe br_netfilter

sudo tee /etc/sysctl.d/99-kubernetes.conf > /dev/null <<'EOF'
net.ipv4.ip_forward = 1
net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables = 1
net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-ip6tables = 1
EOF
sudo sysctl --load=/etc/sysctl.d/99-kubernetes.conf

lsmod | grep -E '^(overlay|br_netfilter)\b'
sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-ip6tables

Overlay supports layered container filesystems. Bridge netfilter allows filtering of bridged traffic; requirements depend on the eventual network plugin. IPv4 forwarding permits routing between interfaces. The files persist the settings; modprobe and sysctl apply them immediately. Both modules and three values of 1 were observed. Persistence after a further reboot has not yet been demonstrated.

docs.title: 6. Install CRI-O
docs.text:
Podman builds and tests images directly. CRI-O serves Kubernetes' Container Runtime Interface (CRI), managing containers requested by the kubelet. They have different roles and can coexist. This lab selected the 1.36 CRI-O and Kubernetes series.

sudo tee /etc/yum.repos.d/cri-o.repo > /dev/null <<'EOF'
[cri-o]
name=CRI-O v1.36
baseurl=https://download.opensuse.org/repositories/isv:/cri-o:/stable:/v1.36/rpm/
enabled=1
gpgcheck=1
gpgkey=https://download.opensuse.org/repositories/isv:/cri-o:/stable:/v1.36/rpm/repodata/repomd.xml.key
EOF
sudo dnf makecache --refresh --disablerepo='*' --enablerepo=cri-o
sudo dnf list --showduplicates cri-o
sudo dnf install cri-o container-selinux --assumeno
sudo dnf install cri-o container-selinux
rpm -q cri-o container-selinux podman
crio --version
sudo systemctl enable --now crio
systemctl is-enabled crio
systemctl is-active crio

The preview selected cri-o 1.36.7-150500.1.1, with container-selinux already installed and no removals. Initially only the preview was run, so crio: command not found and missing service errors followed. Running the actual installation resolved this. The user reported CRI-O installed, enabled and active; the later Kubernetes screenshot independently shows its active service state. A captured post-install crio --version result is still absent.

docs.title: Red Hat subscription warning
docs.text:
DNF displayed a registered-but-not-receiving-updates warning. It was investigated separately from CRI-O's community repository:

sudo subscription-manager identity
sudo subscription-manager status
sudo subscription-manager refresh
sudo subscription-manager repos --list-enabled
sudo dnf makecache --refresh --disablerepo='*' --enablerepo=rhel-9-for-x86_64-baseos-rpms --enablerepo=rhel-9-for-x86_64-appstream-rpms
sudo dnf check-update --disablerepo='*' --enablerepo=rhel-9-for-x86_64-baseos-rpms --enablerepo=rhel-9-for-x86_64-appstream-rpms
printf 'DNF exit code: %s\n' "$?"

The user reported successful metadata refresh and update checking. That confirms repository access at the time of testing, not that the warning disappeared. Under Simple Content Access, Disabled status alone is not proof of lost access; the actual status output was not supplied. No subscription UUIDs are published. DNF check-update returns 0 for no updates, 100 for updates available, 1 for error.

docs.title: 7. Install Kubernetes packages
docs.text:
sudo tee /etc/yum.repos.d/kubernetes.repo > /dev/null <<'EOF'
[kubernetes]
name=Kubernetes v1.36
baseurl=https://pkgs.k8s.io/core:/stable:/v1.36/rpm/
enabled=1
gpgcheck=1
gpgkey=https://pkgs.k8s.io/core:/stable:/v1.36/rpm/repodata/repomd.xml.key
exclude=kubelet kubeadm kubectl cri-tools kubernetes-cni
EOF
sudo dnf makecache --refresh --disablerepo='*' --enablerepo=kubernetes
sudo dnf install kubelet kubeadm kubectl cri-tools --disableexcludes=kubernetes

The exclusion prevents ordinary DNF updates from unexpectedly upgrading these packages. The explicit override permits this planned installation. Package signature verification stays enabled. This command selects the available patch from the 1.36 stream; it is not an exact historical patch pin for future rebuilds.

rpm -q kubelet kubeadm kubectl cri-tools
kubeadm version -o short
kubelet --version
kubectl version --client
crictl --version
sudo systemctl enable kubelet
systemctl is-enabled kubelet
systemctl is-active crio
Component Observed version/state Purpose kubeadm 1.36.5 Bootstraps and joins nodes kubelet 1.36.5; enabled Node agent kubectl 1.36.5 Kubernetes API client cri-tools 1.36.0 Runtime diagnostics via crictl kubernetes-cni 1.9.1 Network-plugin binaries; not a deployed cluster network CRI-O service active Node container runtime

Enabling kubelet schedules startup at boot; this is not evidence of a running control plane. Subsequent kubeadm initialisation is recorded in the next guide; worker joins remain pending.

docs.title: Runtime communication (subsequently verified)
docs.text:
These checks were subsequently completed; see the evidence:

sudo tee /etc/crictl.yaml > /dev/null <<'EOF'
runtime-endpoint: unix:///var/run/crio/crio.sock
image-endpoint: unix:///var/run/crio/crio.sock
timeout: 10
debug: false
EOF
sudo crictl version
sudo crictl info
sudo crictl ps -a

This configures the diagnostic client, not kubelet. Expected evidence is CRI-O responding with CRI API v1 and RuntimeReady true. NetworkReady may be false before CNI configuration. An empty container list is normal before bootstrap. Firewall rules, Pod/Service address ranges, CNI selection, runtime/cgroup checks and SELinux compatibility must be settled before cluster initialisation.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• Kubernetes 1.36 kubeadm installation
  • CRI-O packaging
  • crictl diagnostics
  • Red Hat Simple Content Access status

docs.title: CI and local registry plan
docs.text:
Status: selected architecture, not deployed. Updated 2026-10-14.

The source repository stays on GitHub. A self-hosted GitHub Actions runner and a local container registry will share one supporting RHEL VM outside Kubernetes. VM name, address, storage allocation and executor details remain to be configured.

GitHub repository and Actions workflow
             |
             v
Supporting RHEL VM
  Runner: test code, build images with Podman
             |
             v
  Local registry: persist and serve built images
             |
             v
Kubernetes nodes: kubelet -> CRI-O -> application containers

The runner connects outbound to GitHub for jobs and pushes images locally. There is no need to publish the registry to the internet. Cluster nodes independently need network access, certificate trust and pull credentials for the registry. GitHub stores source code; the registry stores built images. Publishing an image does not deploy it: an explicit deployment workflow will update Kubernetes.

CNCF Distribution is the proposed initial registry, hosted with Podman and persistent storage, HTTPS and authentication. Harbor remains an optional later exercise. Co-location conserves laptop resources but couples registry availability and security to the build VM; keep it running when nodes need image pulls.

Build pipelines should start with one concurrent job. Before registering a runner for this public repository, restrict which workflows can execute on it: do not run untrusted fork pull-request code on the persistent lab runner. Registry and deployment credentials must stay outside Git, with narrowly scoped access.

GitLab Runner, Jenkins and Kubernetes-executor CI Pods were explored as learning alternatives. They are not the selected local implementation. This is a personal lab design, not a claim about any employer's deployed architecture.

Next: finish the Kubernetes foundation, then provision the supporting VM and verify a local image push/pull before automating it through GitHub Actions.

docs.title: Control-plane bootstrap and Calico networking
docs.text: Recorded 2026-10-14. Commands run inside the RHEL VM. Historical creation commands are not instructions to recreate an existing cluster.

docs.title: Verified outcome and remaining work
docs.text:
Kubernetes 1.36.5 initialised successfully on lab-control-01. The API server, etcd, controller manager, scheduler and kube-proxy were Running. The node was NotReady and both CoreDNS Pods were Pending before the Pod network was installed. The Calico 3.33.0 operator subsequently reached 1/1 Running with no restarts.

Subsequent verification confirmed the node Ready, both CoreDNS Pods Running, and Calico Available with no degradation. The IP pool and internal/external Pod DNS lookups were reported correct. See the verification update below. Worker joins, cross-node connectivity and application deployments remain pending. The bootstrap-success screenshot contains a join token and is excluded from public evidence; the non-sensitive results above were transcribed instead.

docs.title: Runtime and address verification
docs.text:
sudo crictl version
sudo crictl info
sudo crictl ps -a
sudo crictl images
hostname
getent ahostsv4 lab-control-01
ip -br address
ip -4 route

crictl talks directly to CRI-O through the configured Unix socket. It reported CRI-O 1.36.7, CRI API v1 and RuntimeReady true. NetworkReady false reported no CNI configuration; this was expected before installing the network. Empty container/image lists were historical results before bootstrap.

Network Range Purpose Hyper-V VM network 192.168.200.0/24 Node addresses; gateway 192.168.200.1 Pod network 10.244.0.0/16 Application Pod addresses managed by Calico Service network 10.96.0.0/12 Kubernetes virtual Service addresses

These ranges do not overlap the known local networks. Future VPN routes must also be checked before connecting the lab to additional networks.

docs.title: Firewall and host preparation
docs.text:
Initially, firewalld rich rules allowed TCP 6443 from the VM and Pod networks, and TCP 10250 from the VM network. Runtime/permanent rules matched and SSH remained allowed. This intermediate configuration is preserved as history.

The subsequent Calico preparation followed its requirements to disable firewalld, which can interfere with Calico-managed rules. The configuration was backed up under /root/firewalld-before-calico-<timestamp>. Those earlier rules are no longer enforced by firewalld. SELinux remains Enforcing. No Calico host endpoint policies have been configured; Pod policies do not automatically replace host protection. This is a private Hyper-V lab, not a production firewall design.

sudo tee /etc/NetworkManager/conf.d/calico.conf > /dev/null <<'EOF'
[keyfile]
unmanaged-devices=interface-name:cali*;interface-name:tunl*;interface-name:vxlan.calico;interface-name:vxlan-v6.calico;interface-name:wireguard.cali;interface-name:wg-v6.cali
EOF
sudo nmcli general reload
nmcli device status
sudo tee /etc/modules-load.d/calico.conf > /dev/null <<'EOF'
vxlan
EOF
sudo modprobe vxlan
sudo systemctl disable --now firewalld
systemctl is-enabled firewalld
systemctl is-active firewalld
getenforce
ip -4 route

NetworkManager must leave Calico interfaces alone. The VXLAN module enables encapsulated inter-node Pod traffic; its node-to-node transport uses UDP 4789. Observed results: module loaded, firewalld disabled/inactive, SELinux Enforcing, eth0 connected and the default route unchanged.

docs.title: Bootstrap verification
docs.text:
The guest configuration at ~/cluster-bootstrap/kubeadm-init.yaml selected Kubernetes v1.36.5, API endpoint 192.168.200.10:6443, CRI-O socket unix:///var/run/crio/crio.sock, the networks above, systemd cgroups and kube-proxy iptables mode.

kubeadm config validate --config ~/cluster-bootstrap/kubeadm-init.yaml
sudo kubeadm config images pull --config "$HOME/cluster-bootstrap/kubeadm-init.yaml"
sudo crictl images
sudo kubeadm init phase preflight --config "$HOME/cluster-bootstrap/kubeadm-init.yaml"

Validation returned ok and images downloaded. Preflight completed with warnings: the vendor 5.14 kernel was not in the upstream LTS list, hostname DNS lookup failed, and CRI-O's pause 3.10.1 differed from kubeadm's 3.10.2. Hostname and pause image corrections were proposed, but separate confirmation of those corrections was not supplied. Successful bootstrap does not prove every warning was cleared or establish production support for this combination.

The subsequent command completed successfully; do not rerun it:

sudo kubeadm init --config "$HOME/cluster-bootstrap/kubeadm-init.yaml"

The administrator configured kubectl locally and inspected the cluster:

mkdir -p "$HOME/.kube"
sudo install -o "$(id -u)" -g "$(id -g)" -m 600 \
  /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf "$HOME/.kube/config"
kubectl cluster-info
kubectl get nodes -o wide
kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide

Keep the generated kubeconfig and join tokens out of Git. At this stage the control-plane containers were Running; node readiness awaited networking.

docs.title: Operator installation
docs.text:
Calico v3.33.0 manifests were downloaded from the pinned upstream tag into ~/cluster-bootstrap/calico. The v3 CRDs were created before the operator:

kubectl create -f v3_projectcalico_org.yaml
kubectl create -f tigera-operator.yaml
kubectl rollout status deployment/tigera-operator -n tigera-operator --timeout=180s
kubectl get pods -n tigera-operator -o wide
kubectl get events -n tigera-operator --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp

The rollout succeeded, with 1/1 Running and normal image-pull/start events. Operator readiness alone does not establish Pod-network readiness.

docs.title: Configure VXLAN (subsequently completed)
docs.text:
Copy the contents of the prepared Installation manifest to ~/cluster-bootstrap/calico/calico-installation.yaml in the VM.

  • bgp: Disabled disables BGP route exchange.
  • encapsulation: VXLAN uses VXLAN for cross-node traffic, including nodes on the same subnet; this is not the CrossSubnet setting.
  • cidr matches the kubeadm Pod subnet. /26 is an allocation block size, not a limit of 64 Pods for the entire cluster.
  • natOutgoing: Enabled translates outgoing Pod traffic to destinations outside Calico IP pools so the external network can return traffic to the node.
  • linuxDataplane: Iptables retains the selected dataplane and kube-proxy.

Validate against the installed API, then apply only if validation succeeds:

cd ~/cluster-bootstrap/calico
kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f calico-installation.yaml && \
  kubectl apply -f calico-installation.yaml
kubectl get installation.operator.tigera.io default
kubectl get tigerastatus
kubectl get pods -n calico-system -o wide

Allow reconciliation and image downloads, then inspect:

kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready node/lab-control-01 --timeout=180s
kubectl get nodes -o wide
kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide
kubectl get tigerastatus
sudo crictl info

A timeout calls for inspecting events and operator status, not rerunning kubeadm init. Node Ready, RuntimeReady/NetworkReady true and healthy system Pods are targets that were subsequently met, as recorded below. Cross-node connectivity requires workers and later tests. Optional observability components are deferred.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• Calico requirements
  • Operator installation
  • Installation API
  • NetworkManager preparation

docs.title: Verification update: networking ready
docs.text:
Fresh terminal output showed lab-control-01 Ready, Kubernetes v1.36.5 and CRI-O 1.36.7. Both CoreDNS Pods were 1/1 Running with zero restarts, at 10.244.242.3 and 10.244.242.4. Calico reported Available True, Progressing False, Degraded False; IP pools and tiers also reported all objects available.

Earlier FailedScheduling and connection-refused probe events were historical. The later Ready conditions and available components demonstrate recovery; no restart was required. Image downloads took time during startup.

The Installation resource confirms BGP Disabled, VXLAN encapsulation, Pod CIDR 10.244.0.0/16, outgoing NAT Enabled and the Iptables dataplane.

The original inspection command used the legacy ippools.crd.projectcalico.org resource and failed. This installation uses native v3 resources. Correct commands:

kubectl api-resources --api-group=projectcalico.org
kubectl get ippools.projectcalico.org \
  -o custom-columns='NAME:.metadata.name,CIDR:.spec.cidr,VXLAN:.spec.vxlanMode,IPIP:.spec.ipipMode,NAT:.spec.natOutgoing'

The user reported the resulting pool was correct. The API-name error was not a network failure. See Calico native v3 CRDs.

docs.title: Pod DNS test and cleanup
docs.text:
A temporary BusyBox 1.37.0 Pod named dns-check in default used a control-plane NoSchedule toleration, without changing the node taint. Service-account token mounting was disabled; resource requests were 10m CPU/16Mi RAM and limits 100m CPU/64Mi RAM. It ran sleep 3600 to allow these checks:

kubectl exec -n default dns-check -- cat /etc/resolv.conf
kubectl exec -n default dns-check -- nslookup kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local
kubectl exec -n default dns-check -- nslookup www.redhat.com
kubectl delete pod dns-check -n default --ignore-not-found=true
kubectl get pod dns-check -n default --ignore-not-found=true

Both internal and external DNS lookups succeeded, and deletion was confirmed by the user. Full lookup answers were not supplied, so no specific resolved addresses are claimed. These checks verify single-node Pod DNS, not cross-node VXLAN traffic or network-policy enforcement.

Next: create and install the first worker.

docs.title: First worker VM: creation and installation preparation
docs.text: Created 2026-10-14; updated 2026-10-15 (Africa/Nairobi). Commands run in Windows PowerShell as Administrator unless labelled RHEL. VM creation below is historical: do not rerun it against the existing worker.

docs.title: Verified state
docs.text:
lab-worker-01 was created Off and has since booted installed RHEL 9.8. It has Generation 2, two virtual CPUs and fixed 5120 MiB RAM. Secure Boot is On using MicrosoftUEFICertificateAuthority. Its network adapter uses reservoir-lab-switch, and its new 40 GB dynamically expanding disk is C:\Users\USER\HyperV\data-platform-lab\lab-worker-01\os.vhdx. The creation and configuration results were supplied as terminal text.

Installer completion and installed-system login are confirmed. The network was subsequently repaired, time synchronisation verified and registration completed. The package update is in progress; completion and post-update reboot are not yet verified. The worker has not joined Kubernetes. ISO ejection was instructed but not separately evidenced. This is a fresh installation, not a control-plane clone.

docs.title: Capacity checks
docs.text:
Before creation, the host reported 31.67 GiB total RAM, 15.2 GiB free RAM and 172.1 GiB free on C:. The control-plane VM was Running with two CPUs and 3 GiB assigned. Its DVD path was blank, and the lab switch was Internal.

Get-VM | Select-Object Name, State, ProcessorCount,
    @{Name='AssignedGiB';Expression={[math]::Round($_.MemoryAssigned / 1GB, 2)}}
Get-VMHost | Select-Object VirtualMachinePath, VirtualHardDiskPath
Get-VMDvdDrive -VMName "lab-control-01" | Format-List VMName, Path
Get-VMSwitch -Name "reservoir-lab-switch" | Select-Object Name, SwitchType

These checks establish available resources and the existing network. Free memory and disk values are a snapshot, not a permanent reservation.

docs.title: Create and configure (completed)
docs.text:
$workerName = "lab-worker-01"
$workerPath = "C:\Users\USER\HyperV\data-platform-lab\lab-worker-01"
$workerDisk = Join-Path $workerPath "os.vhdx"
if (Get-VM -Name $workerName -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
    throw "Worker VM already exists. Inspect it before continuing."
}
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $workerPath) {
    throw "Worker folder already exists. Inspect it before continuing."
}
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $workerPath -ErrorAction Stop
New-VM -Name $workerName -Generation 2 -MemoryStartupBytes 5GB `
    -Path $workerPath -NewVHDPath $workerDisk -NewVHDSizeBytes 40GB `
    -SwitchName "reservoir-lab-switch" -ErrorAction Stop
Set-VMMemory -VMName $workerName -DynamicMemoryEnabled $false -StartupBytes 5GB
Set-VMProcessor -VMName $workerName -Count 2
Set-VMFirmware -VMName $workerName -EnableSecureBoot On `
    -SecureBootTemplate "MicrosoftUEFICertificateAuthority"
Set-VM -Name $workerName -AutomaticStopAction ShutDown

Generation 2 provides UEFI firmware. Fixed memory avoids the earlier control-plane Dynamic Memory issue. The virtual disk grows as data is written, up to 40 GB. The certificate-authority template supports Linux bootloaders. ShutDown requests a graceful guest shutdown when the host shuts down.

Get-VM -Name $workerName | Select-Object Name, State, Generation, ProcessorCount
Get-VMMemory -VMName $workerName | Select-Object DynamicMemoryEnabled,
    @{Name='StartupMiB';Expression={$_.Startup / 1MB}}
Get-VMFirmware -VMName $workerName | Select-Object SecureBoot, SecureBootTemplate
Get-VMNetworkAdapter -VMName $workerName | Select-Object VMName, SwitchName
Get-VMHardDiskDrive -VMName $workerName | Format-List VMName, Path

Observed: Off, Generation 2, two CPUs, DynamicMemoryEnabled False, 5120 MiB, Secure Boot On with the chosen template, correct switch and disk path.

docs.title: Locate ISO and boot installer (historical instructions)
docs.text:
The earlier control-plane installation used the verified RHEL 9.8 x86_64 DVD ISO in Downloads. Confirm it still exists before attaching it:

$workerName = "lab-worker-01"
$rhelIso = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE "Downloads\rhel-9.8-x86_64-dvd.iso"
Test-Path -LiteralPath $rhelIso
Get-Item -LiteralPath $rhelIso -ErrorAction Stop | Select-Object FullName, Length

If missing, search Downloads and use the actual returned path:

Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads" `
    -Filter "*rhel*.iso" -File -Recurse | Select-Object FullName

Once confirmed, attach the media and place DVD first in the boot order:

$workerDvd = Get-VMDvdDrive -VMName $workerName
if ($workerDvd) {
    $workerDvd | Set-VMDvdDrive -Path $rhelIso -ErrorAction Stop
} else {
    Add-VMDvdDrive -VMName $workerName -Path $rhelIso -ErrorAction Stop
}
$workerDvd = Get-VMDvdDrive -VMName $workerName
Set-VMFirmware -VMName $workerName -FirstBootDevice $workerDvd -ErrorAction Stop
Get-VMDvdDrive -VMName $workerName | Format-List VMName, Path
(Get-VMFirmware -VMName $workerName).BootOrder |
    Format-Table BootType, Description -AutoSize
vmconnect.exe localhost $workerName

In Virtual Machine Connection, click Start, respond to the DVD boot prompt if shown, and select Install Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.8. Choose English (United States) and continue to Installation Summary. The user subsequently confirmed reaching Installation Summary and completing installation. The following sections record first boot and network repair.

docs.title: First boot and connectivity repair
docs.text:
The installed worker reported hostname lab-worker-01, RHEL 9.8, about 4.5 GiB usable RAM and 4 GiB swap. sudo whoami returned root. SSH access was reported working, but subsequent console diagnostics showed that Ethernet had lost its IPv4 configuration. The exact cause of that transition is not established.

The corrected ip -4 route command returned no routes. eth0 was UP without an IP address, and nmcli connection show --active listed only loopback. DNS servers were present in resolv.conf but unreachable without working networking. This was more than a DNS configuration problem.

The following commands created or reused a dedicated profile in the worker's Hyper-V console. Existing profiles were preserved:

if ! nmcli connection show "lab-worker-eth0" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  sudo nmcli connection add type ethernet \
    con-name "lab-worker-eth0" ifname eth0 \
    connection.autoconnect no
fi
sudo nmcli connection modify "lab-worker-eth0" \
  connection.interface-name eth0 \
  connection.autoconnect yes \
  connection.autoconnect-priority 100 \
  ipv4.method manual \
  ipv4.addresses "192.168.200.11/24" \
  ipv4.gateway "192.168.200.1" \
  ipv4.dns "1.1.1.1 8.8.8.8" \
  ipv4.ignore-auto-dns yes \
  ipv4.never-default no
sudo nmcli connection up "lab-worker-eth0"
ip -br address
ip -4 route
nmcli connection show --active
ping -c 3 -W 2 192.168.200.1
getent ahostsv4 www.redhat.com
curl -I --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 30 https://www.redhat.com

The profile activated on eth0, the gateway replied, DNS resolved the hostname, and HTTPS returned HTTP/2 301. Earlier curl errors omitted the numeric argument after --max-time; the final command corrected that. The success screenshot contains HTTP cookies and is excluded from public images. Autoconnect is configured, but persistence after a further reboot has not yet been retested.

docs.title: Time synchronisation and registration
docs.text:
Chrony selected a time source, reported Leap status Normal, and timedatectl reported System clock synchronized yes with NTP active in Africa/Nairobi. An earlier 501 Not authorised likely resulted from running the mutating chronyc online command without sudo. The correct form is shown below; no additional retry was needed once synchronisation was confirmed.

sudo systemctl enable --now chronyd
sudo chronyc online
chronyc sources -v
chronyc tracking
timedatectl
hostnamectl --static
sudo subscription-manager register

Enter Red Hat account credentials interactively. The first registration attempt reported invalid credentials; the second succeeded for lab-worker-01. The registration screenshots contain a system ID and account identifier and are not published. No passwords or registration IDs are recorded here.

docs.title: Package update (in progress)
docs.text:
These batches were provided after registration. The user subsequently reported that the worker was updating. Detailed repository and transaction completion output has not yet been supplied:

sudo subscription-manager refresh
sudo subscription-manager repos \
  --enable=rhel-9-for-x86_64-baseos-rpms \
  --enable=rhel-9-for-x86_64-appstream-rpms
sudo dnf repolist --enabled
sudo dnf makecache --refresh
sudo dnf upgrade --refresh

Refresh retrieves account information; BaseOS and AppStream supply system and application packages. makecache checks metadata access, while upgrade installs available package updates after confirmation.

Only after DNF finishes successfully, reboot and verify:

sudo reboot

Reconnect from Windows with ssh sabare@192.168.200.11, then run:

hostnamectl --static
uname -r
ip -br address
ip -4 route
free -h
swapon --show
timedatectl

Next: verify the updated kernel and persistent networking, disable swap persistently, prepare kernel networking and install the compatible Kubernetes runtime and tools. None of those worker preparation steps or cluster join is claimed complete yet.

docs.title: Progress and evidence register
docs.text:
Updated: 2026-10-15 (Africa/Nairobi).

This register records user-shared terminal output and completion reports. It is not an independent live audit of the Hyper-V host. Selected original screenshots are embedded in the installation and first-boot guides. They show only the personal lab; credentials, cookie-bearing HTTP output and unrelated personal storage-cleanup material are not included.

The screenshot index lists all 33 included images, their purposes and the reasons other supplied images were not published.

docs.title: Resolved symptom, unknown cause
docs.text: Switch creation initially failed with 0x800700B7. Read-only switch, adapter and Plug and Play inspections did not identify a conflicting lab device. A retry later succeeded. A restart was suggested but not confirmed. The root cause must remain unknown rather than being presented as a proven fix.

docs.title: Decisions and open questions
docs.text:
• Use Hyper-V as the local substitute for infrastructure-provided VMs.
  • Run upstream Kubernetes inside the RHEL guests, not on OpenShift Local.
  • RHEL 9.8 chosen for this lab; reference environment version still unknown.
  • Server selected without GUI or optional add-ons; administer through terminal/SSH.
  • Guest address 192.168.200.10/24 with gateway 192.168.200.1; public DNS for the home lab.
  • Root password set privately; root password SSH was instructed off and needs verification.
  • Disk layout verified: EFI, XFS boot, LVM root and swap; swap disabled without deleting its volume.
  • CRI-O 1.36 selected; Kubernetes 1.36.5 packages installed. Calico 3.33.0 selected with VXLAN and BGP disabled.
  • Podman is intended for image workflows, not as the Kubernetes CRI runtime.
  • One control plane initially; high availability is not provided.
  • Add services incrementally within laptop capacity.
  • Public evidence must use synthetic data and omit credentials/internal documents.
  • Satellite/package mirroring was discussed for understanding, not added to scope.
  • Read-only MCP is deferred until Kubernetes is operational.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Finish the worker package update, reboot and verify its kernel and network persistence. Then prepare swap, kernel networking, CRI-O and Kubernetes tools before joining the cluster. See first worker VM. Cross-node networking remains untested; the second worker and runner/registry VM remain planned.

docs.text:
• Password-entry screens and output containing HTTP cookies are not published. The relevant configuration and HTTPS result are described in text instead.
